core.title: Declare each train's family (behavior or delivery) to match its terminal contract
core.given: A train definition (a plan artifact) exists or is being written: it is authored, edited (family, terminal contract or train ID added, changed or removed), or reviewed/validated even if unchanged.
core.when: The planner sets, adds or corrects a train's family; adds, changes or removes its terminal contract; proposes or changes a train ID; or reviews/validates existing train definitions.
core.then: Declare family as delivery if and only if the declared terminal contract requires a durable Acceptance Authority commit and terminates in the acceptance-commit receipt (the profile's commit-receipt URN); otherwise declare behavior.
prefer: Derive family from the terminal contract (the source of truth); family is its validator-checked assertion, so re-derive it whenever the terminal contract changes.
behavior: observe, exercise, classify, validate, recommend or report a capability against a system under examination; no authority commit.
delivery: govern accepted-system state through a durable Acceptance Authority commit.
avoid: Encoding family in the train ID (never an ID digit).
Omitting family (mandatory) or treating it as a second source of truth that diverges from the terminal contract.
Inferring family from the variant category (values 0-3) or vice versa; the axes are orthogonal.
core.why: Behavior trains only exercise a capability; delivery trains change accepted-system state via an authority commit. Deriving family from the terminal contract keeps this checkable and out of IDs and variant categories.
evidence: The family check passes: every train's family equals the family derived from its declared terminal contract.
Every train definition has a family field with value behavior or delivery.
No train ID encodes the family.
verification: Derivation: a terminal contract that requires a durable Acceptance Authority commit AND terminates in the profile's commit-receipt URN => delivery; any other terminal contract => behavior.
Allowed family values: behavior | delivery. Schema shape: train -> {family, definition}; family is mandatory.

Missing family, or a family that mismatches the family derived from the declared terminal contract, is a finding; the check runs on all train definitions, not only changed ones, so unchanged definitions under review or validation can fail it.

Not covered: the check does not cross-check family against the variant-category axis (values 0-3; the two axes are orthogonal), and it does not itself verify that train IDs omit the family (kept in avoid; an independent obligation is suggested for it).

values: train family missing or mismatching the family derived from its terminal contract

fires: A planner authors a new train definition and must set its family.
A planner adds, changes or removes a train's terminal contract (for example to or away from one returning the acceptance-commit receipt), even without touching family.
A planner corrects an existing train's family value, or adds a missing family field, without changing the terminal contract.
A planner reviews or validates existing train definitions that were not edited, and must check each family is present and matches its terminal contract.
A planner proposes or changes train IDs, including a scheme that encodes behavior/delivery as a digit.
doesNotFire: Choosing only the variant category (0-3) of a train without touching, reviewing or validating family, terminal contract or train ID.
Editing wagon or WMBT (plan-artifact) content that does not change, review or validate any train's terminal contract, family or ID.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds of the stack, so the file_kind fact and the check can recognize train definitions as plan artifacts.
The URN of the Acceptance Authority's commit receipt that a delivery train's terminal contract terminates in; the derivation of family = delivery depends on it.

proposedKeys.meaning: The URN of the Acceptance Authority's commit receipt that a delivery train's terminal contract terminates in; used to derive family = delivery.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.acceptance (and the other urn.<artifact> keys) describe an artifact's own URN shape or binding syntax; no existing key describes the receipt URN that a terminal contract terminates in.

neutralityNotes: Train, family, terminal contract, Acceptance Authority, variant category (including its method-level 0-3 value range), wagon and WMBT are ATDD-method concepts (train/wmbt/wagon appear in the closed vocabulary's artifact params) and remain in the core, as does the method's train schema shape train -> {family, definition} in core verification. The only stack-concrete datum the core needs is the commit-receipt URN; the closed vocabulary has no key for it, so urn.commit_receipt is proposed and listed in profileRequirements. Realization details kept in bunOnly: the validator/finding id planner.train.family-matches-terminal-contract and the sibling rule id planner.train.categories. The concrete receipt-URN example inside fires[1] was neutralized to 'the acceptance-commit receipt' (bun.json itself ships as the reference example). unless is empty in the realization and stays empty in the core. No per-rule severity or disposition is declared in bun.json, so none was added.
